Subject: Private deployment: allowlist & outbound controls for tenant 'acme-prod'

Hi Marissa,

We're getting close to the private deployment kickoff for our 'acme-prod' tenant (VPC peering + on-prem proxy). Our security team needs a concise list of IPs, ports, and firewall behaviors we must include in the allowlist and the expected egress behavior from Redwood's Private control plane and from any customer-side agents. Can you provide a short checklist and any templates we can drop into our ticketing system?

Specific asks from Security:
- Static IP ranges for control-plane callbacks and telemetry (if any)
- Source ports and destination ports to allow from the deployment hosts
- Whether TLS termination or SNI-based routing is required
- Expected DNS resolution patterns and any special domains to allow
- If we need to NAT/route through a dedicated egress IP, do you require IP assertion on client side?

Appreciate anything concise — our auditors want to triage this in the next 48 hours.

Thanks,
Luke Peterson
Senior InfoSec Engineer
Acme Health

Hi Marissa / team —

Below is a compact, auditor-friendly checklist we can send to Acme. I also attached a filled CSV template for their ops team. Key points first, then technical rationale:

One-page checklist (summary):
- Control plane API endpoints (HTTPS, outbound from customer network to Redwood):
  - 52.23.150.0/24
  - 34.198.72.0/24
  - Destination: TCP 443 (HTTPS)
  - TLS: required; SNI must match "control.redwood-inference.com"
- Data-plane egress (model inference traffic / KV prefetch):
  - Connections initiated from customer hosts (model workers) to Redwood runtime ingress:
  - 18.205.45.0/24 (primary)
  - 3.210.60.0/24 (failover)
  - Destination: TCP 443 for inference APIs; allow persistent TLS sessions
- Metrics/telemetry & callbacks:
  - telemetry.redwood-inference.com (CNAME -> dynamic IPs); allow outbound HTTPS to FQDN; if only IPs allowed, see ranges above (same as control plane).
- Outbound DNS / TLS considerations:
  - Allow outbound DNS (UDP 53) from deployment control hosts to their designated resolvers.
  - For lock-down environments, allow DNS over TLS to resolver IPs.
- NAT / egress topology:
  - Recommended: route Redwood-bound traffic through a dedicated NAT gateway with static egress IP(s) that you provide; we will accept assertion of tenant-bound egress IPs for firewall rules.
  - If you cannot NAT, we can support per-worker dynamic IP ranges but recommend NAT for stable allowlisting.
- Inbound requirements: none. Redwood Private does not require inbound holes; all control and model requests are outbound from your VPC to Redwood endpoints.
- Ports to allow (source -> dest):
  - Src: ephemeral (>1024) -> Dest: 443 (HTTPS)
  - Src: ephemeral -> Dest: 853 (DNS over TLS) if used
- Session characteristics & timeouts:
  - Long-lived TLS sessions for inference to allow KV cache reuse and reduce latency. Idle timeouts should be >= 15 minutes for worker pools.
- Failover / fallback behavior:
  - If primary data-plane IPs are unreachable, traffic will failover to the listed failover CIDR. If both are unreachable, we provide a policy for degraded mode (rate-limited queued requests) — ops must enable a trust policy.

Attachments referenced: redwood_allowlist_template.csv (populated), and a short note explaining each column.

Notes / Rationale (brief):
- We use TLS and SNI for multi-tenant control-plane routing; firewall rules keyed to FQDN are OK but many auditors require IPs, so we provide both.
- Persistent TLS sessions reduce per-request overhead and preserve KV caches; recommend allowing long-lived connections from worker hosts.
- No inbound firewall openings required on the customer side.

Operational asks for Acme (to include in ticket):
- Provide your NAT public IP(s) for allowlisting, or confirm you'll maintain the NAT pool and accept dynamic ranges.
- List your internal resolver behavior (standard DNS vs DoT) and whether firewall allows outbound UDP 53.
- Confirm which CIDRs in your network will host the worker nodes so we can correlate with our audit.

If this looks good I can convert to a one-page PDF and populate the CSV template for them.

--
Dev Patel
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood-inference.com
[Attachment: redwood_allowlist_template.csv]

3) Once you confirm the NAT IP(s) we'll add them to your firewall request and sign off with security. If your auditors need an official security note on telemetry retention or TLS ciphers, Jonas and I can produce a short attestation.

> Data-plane primary: 18.205.45.0/24; failover: 3.210.60.0/24 — destination TCP 443; permit long-lived TLS sessions (idle >= 15m).
